newsitem.title: USA: United Tech taps Otis vet for China venture.
newsitem.headline: United Tech taps Otis vet for China venture.

text.p: Andrea Vecchiotti recently retired as Otis Elevator's Asia-Pacific technology transfer director, but he plans to spend his "retirement" helping the United Technologies Corp unit fight for market share in China.
Vecchiotti, 65, told Reuters he will serve as advisor to an unspecified joint venture Otis is planning for China.

China is a key industry battleground. A spokeswoman said Otis holds between 20-25 percent of the market, in a virtual tie with rivals Mitsubishi Electric Corp of Japan and Schindler Holding AG of Switzerland.

The spokeswoman said Otis, the world's largest elevator manufacturer, will reveal details of the venture by the end of the first quarter. The company has already invested $70 million in four joint ventures in China since 1984.

China accounts for about five percent of Otis' $5.3 billion in annual revenues, and the figure should grow to 10 percent by early in the next century, said Jean-Pierre van Rooy, president of Farmington, Conn-based Otis.
"I think our Chinese company will one day be the biggest company at Otis," van Rooy said.
Otis sells about 41,000 elevators and escalators a year, and more than half of its new-equipment installations are now in Asia, said van Rooy.
China accounts for more than 4,000 of the company's total 68,000 employees around the world.

For the new venture, Otis is tapping an experienced manager in Vecchiotti, who has held key manufacturing and engineering posts at Otis in Europe, Latin America and Asia. He served in seven countries after joining Otis as a 15-year-old apprentice in his native Milan, Italy, in 1946.
Vecchiotti first went to China in 1987, helping transform what he called "primitive" production methods in Tianjin.
He said that while elevator technology had changed dramatically during his half-century in the business, not all the changes were visible.
"What you see in the cab is not that different. Most of the change has been in the controls, in what you don't see," he said.
